bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav Flags Bihar Fiscal Deficit, Rising Debt | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 21, 2026 Bihar's Fiscal Deficit Touches 5.8%, Tejashwi Yadav Raises Alarm Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Bishnu J Tejashwi Yadav | Image Source: PTI Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Friday, August 21, raised questions over the state's finances, pointing to the rise in public debt and a fiscal deficit of 5.8 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) in 2025-26. In a social media post, the RJD leader said the numbers were worrying and accused the BJP-led NDA government of mishandling the state's finances. Yadav claimed the financial strain was being felt in government payments, alleging delays in payments to employees and pensioners, social security beneficiaries and contractors. He also said it was affecting spending on development work. He further claimed that allocations under the Student Credit Card scheme had been cut and that scholarships were being reduced. Yadav said Bihar's revenue deficit and debt had both increased and questioned the government's plans to improve revenue collection and keep the fiscal deficit under control. He also alleged that the state had taken on a large amount of additional debt over the past two years even as its finances remained under pressure. Calling the situation a "serious financial crisis", Yadav accused the NDA government of corruption and financial mismanagement. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Bhagalpur identifies 100 acres for proposed sugar mill in Pirpainti - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image Bhagalpur: The Bhagalpur district administration has identified around 100 acres of land in Pirpainti for a proposed modern sugar mill, a move aimed at expanding sugarcane cultivation, improving farmers’ incomes and creating local jobs, Jagran reported. District Magistrate Alankrita Pandey said a detailed report on the selected land has been sent to Bihar’s Sugarcane Development Department. The project will move to the next stage after receiving administrative and technical approval from the department. The state Sugarcane Development Department had been searching for suitable land in Bhagalpur for several months following directions from its headquarters. Officials assessed possible sites in Kahalgaon and Pirpainti before selecting the land in Pirpainti based on the required area and other conditions. Pirpainti has the largest area under sugarcane cultivation among the main cane-growing blocks in the district. Sugarcane is also grown in Nathnagar and Sultanganj. The agriculture and sugarcane departments are registering farmers to encourage greater sugarcane cultivation. Registered farmers will be eligible for government support such as improved planting material, farm equipment and financial assistance. The proposed mill is expected to provide farmers in the region with a nearby market for their sugarcane. Direct procurement by the mill could reduce farmers’ dependence on distant buyers and help them avoid selling their produce at low prices. Officials also expect the project to encourage more farmers to take up sugarcane cultivation and increase the area under the crop across the region. The proposed industrial unit is also expected to generate direct and indirect employment and self-employment opportunities for thousands of people once it becomes operational. “District administration has identified 100 acres of land in Pirpainti for setting up the sugar mill. A detailed report has been prepared and sent to the Sugarcane Development Department. Once departmental approval is received, further work will be started quickly,” Pandey said.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar govt clarifies: No cut in student credit card Rs 4 lakh loan limit - EducationTimes.com
bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar government on Friday clarified that students would be able continue availing education loans of up to Rs 4 lakh under the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme. The Bihar State Education Finance Corporation will provide up to Rs 2 lakh, the statement said, while scheduled commercial banks will continue providing the remaining Rs 2 lakh to Rs 4 lakh. As per prior rules, the corporation itself provided loans of up to Rs 4 lakh. The statement came a day after Jan Suraaj functionaries, at a press conference, alleged that the Student Credit Card scheme had been diluted and the maximum loan amount reduced from Rs 4 lakh to Rs 2 lakh. According to a department release, Rajiv Raushan, secretary, higher education, said the change was aimed at expanding the scope of financial assistance for higher education. The scheme has also been linked with the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana, PM Vidyalaxmi portal and banks. Students, meanwhile, can avail education loans of up to Rs 10 lakh through PM Vidyalaxmi. The department said expenditure approval for the scheme had risen from Rs 886 crore in 2025-26 to Rs 950 crore in 2026-27, marking an uptick of Rs 64 crore. It said the figures showed financial assistance had not been reduced but expanded.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Gets 11.19 Lakh Pucca Houses with ₹13,427 Crore Allocation - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Gets 11.19 Lakh Pucca Houses with ₹13,427 Crore Allocation 21 Aug 2026 2 min read Why in News? Union Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced the approval of 11,18,937 pucca houses for poor families in Bihar , along with an allocation of ₹13,427 crore , during a State-level Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana programme in Patna on 20 August 2026 . Key Points: Housing Approval: A total of 11,18,937 pucca houses have been approved for poor families in Bihar. Financial Allocation: The approved housing package involves an allocation of ₹13,427 crore . PM Awas Yojana: The housing initiative aims to provide poor families with secure and dignified living conditions through pucca houses. Two-Year Progress: During the last two years, 24,30,327 houses have been approved for Bihar, involving a total expenditure of ₹29,164 crore . Crop Insurance: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) will now be implemented in Bihar to provide farmers protection against crop losses caused by natural calamities . Risks Covered: Crop insurance will provide protection against risks such as floods, drought, excessive rainfall and other natural calamities , subject to the scheme’s provisions. Women’s Empowerment: The government will focus on creating more Lakhpati Didis through Self-Help Groups, self-employment and group-based enterprises. She-Marts: She-Marts are proposed to be established in every district to provide Jeevika Didis and women’s Self-Help Groups with markets for their products. Rural Connectivity: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was highlighted as an important component of rural development by improving connectivity between villages, markets and essential services. Three Pillars of Rural Development: The government highlighted roads, houses and agriculture as three important pillars for improving rural livelihoods and strengthening the rural economy. national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 177 PM Modi says reforms are not a compulsion but a commitment and conviction for his government
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that reforms are not a compulsion but a commitment and conviction for his government, and that its policies are pro-people, pro-growth and pro-development. Addressing the World Leaders Forum in New Delhi last evening, PM Modi said his government has created a clear roadmap for reforms, with the primary focus being on reforms at the governance level. He said India is undertaking next-generation reforms at the policy level to secure the country’s future. The Prime Minister pointed out that his government is not merely changing regulations but is changing the entire philosophy behind them. He said that earlier, the approach to regulations was Prohibited unless Permitted. PM Modi said the licence raj under earlier governments contributed to unemployment, while his government’s Production Linked Incentive model is creating new opportunities. The Prime Minister also spoke about the global economic environment, saying that the weaponisation of resources and growing mistrust were creating new challenges. He said that even in such circumstances, the world continues to see India as a bright spot of hope and growth. PM Modi said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has forecast that India will remain the world’s fastest-growing major economy. He said India is taking steps that are giving momentum to its development. Highlighting the profound global impact of domestic strength, Mr Modi expressed deep confidence that securing the nation’s development trajectory would inherently bring greater stability to the international community.

national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 158 HM Amit Shah lauds West Bengal govt. for handing over 1,129 acres for India-Bangladesh border fen...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has lauded West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for handing over 1,129 acres of land to the Border Security Force (BSF) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) for fencing along the India-Bangladesh border in the state within 45 days of the new government coming to power. He said the request for the land required for the border fence had been pending since 2014. Mr Shah was speaking while attending a programme at the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) Frontier Headquarters in the Ranidanga area of Siliguri in West Bengal yesterday. The Home Minister said completing border fencing is crucial to stopping infiltration and protecting national security. He said the government will continue its zero-tolerance policy towards illegal immigration. He said the process of identifying, removing and deporting illegal immigrants will be strictly followed. He also said that demographic changes would be strictly prevented. Highlighting the strategic importance of the Siliguri Corridor, also known as the ‘Chicken Neck’, Mr Shah said it is vital for the security of the Northeast and the country. He said the corridor, which connects the Northeast with the rest of the country and is bordered by three countries — Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh — will be protected by a triangular grid of Army posts in Chopra, Dhubri and Kishanganj. On the occasion, he laid foundation stones for infrastructure worth around 189 crore rupees and inaugurated several other projects. Union Home and Cooperation Minister also inaugurated a six-day awareness exhibition on the three new criminal laws, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, at Kawakhali Maidan in Siliguri. Addressing the gathering, Mr Shah said the three new criminal laws will provide greater security to citizens. He announced that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has now been fully implemented in the state and said justice will be ensured within three years of the filing of an FIR. Mr Shah said the new criminal laws, which make extensive use of technology and forensic science, are aimed at ensuring speedy, timely and victim-centric justice. He said the judicial system will be transformed with “three Ts: Technology, Transparency and Timeline”. He said the BJP government under Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari implemented the new laws within three days of assuming office, fulfilling its promise of establishing trust, not fear. He appealed to the people of North Bengal to visit the exhibition. The Home Minister also urged people associated with the justice system, law enforcement and policing in the state to visit the exhibition and familiarise themselves with the new laws. On the occasion, Mr Shah also inaugurated the newly constructed Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate building and a 20-bed drug addiction treatment centre at North Bengal Medical College and Hospital.
